narration.full_text: Namaste students! In this section, we'll dive into the fascinating world of control and coordination in living organisms. We'll explore how different activities are regulated and integrated to ensure survival. Control and coordination is the process by which an organism regulates and integrates its various activities to respond properly to internal and external stimuli. Living organisms constantly perform many activities simultaneously, and these must be controlled and coordinated for balance and survival. All living organisms respond and react to changes in their environment. These changes are called stimuli, which can include light, heat, cold, smell, or touch. Both plants and animals respond to stimuli, but they do so in different ways. In animals, control and coordination are primarily achieved through two main systems: the Nervous system and the Endocrine system. We will learn about each of these in detail.
